newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem says legislative polls next Oct.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem says legislative polls next Oct.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem said in an interview published Tuesday that legislative elections will be held next October.
Opposition parties had hoped to take advantage of a decline in the government's popularity and have the polls earlier next year.
Up for election will be half of the legislators in the lower house of Congress, half of the representatives in one- third of provincial legislatures and, in Buenos Aires, municipal lawmakers.
"We are planning on joint elections for October next year," Menem told La Nacion in an interview.
Menem's popularity has fallen from 50 percent in presidential polls in May 1995 to a current level of about 15 percent, opinion surveys show.
Menem's Peronist party has a majority in the lower house of Congress thanks to alliances with small provincial parties.

He also declined to back any candidate who has announced his intention to run for president in 1999 polls, adding, however, that Buenos Aires province Governor Eduardo Duhalde has "some advantage" because of the high profile of his post.
Menem once again denied speculation of an imminent change in cabinet.
"There is no chance of changes," he said. "We are fine as is so why change?"
